_comment: THE EXEMPLARY SPECIMEN — what a good pack looks like, and the one the SKILL.md walkthrough uses. Its sibling `pack.manifest.json` is the TEST FIXTURE and is deliberately pathological: fourteen board asks, two sections dating differently, two decisions naming the same record. Both ship on purpose, because a specimen cannot be both an exemplar and a fixture and the repo previously asked one file to be both (BL-123, decision D-10 option A). ——— THIS PACK CARRIES FIVE BOARD ASKS, against the five a sitting can take (BOARD_ASK_SITTING in assemble_pack.py), so the over-long warning is SILENT here and fires on the fixture. ——— THE CURATION RULE, applied identically to every section: a board ask stays only where a DATE or a BREACHED THRESHOLD forces it this quarter; everything else the CISO speaks to. Asks were DROPPED, never re-pitched from board to management to get under the number — assemble_pack.py:485 names that failure ('a board decision quietly filed as a management action is a decision nobody took') and hitting five that way would have been the dishonest option. ——— THE FIVE: the cross-cutting through-line ask; posture PR.DS-01 (fund, or accept for two more quarters); risk R-007 (Critical residual OVER APPETITE); exceptions X-001 (November expiry); incident A-002 (due for re-confirmation in April, not re-confirmed, and the exposure has now occurred). ——— `posture` and the through-line point at the PRODUCERS' OWN files unchanged, because they already carried a single board ask and needed no curation. Only the six sections that were cut have a copy under `curated/`, and each copy changes exactly one field — `decisions` — so every section stays consistent with the store it was rendered from.
period: Q3 2026 — SPECIMEN, not a real pack
